courses.title: Python for Beginners
courses.description: Basic concepts of computer software and programming. Numbers, strings, and basic I/O. Expressions, control structures, lists, tuples, and functions. File I/O and introduction to exception handling. Introduction to object-oriented programming. Problem-solving techniques. Cannot be used for CS elective credit.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in MAT 1050 or MAT 1052 .

courses.title: Python for Programmers
courses.description: Python basics. Data structures and control structures. Functions and functional forms. Objects, classes, inheritance, and polymorphism. I/O and exceptions. Advanced features.
courses.prerequisites: CS major and C or better in CS 1400 or CS 1280 ; Data Science minor, AI Minor or Computational Linguistics Minor and C or better in MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , or MAT 1140 ; or Cyber Security minor and C or better in CS 1400 .

courses.title: Fundamentals of Data Science
courses.description: Foundations of data science. Critical concepts and skills in mathematics, statistics and computer programming for data analytics. Fundamental data and file structures to support data analytics. Analysis of real-world datasets. Data privacy and data security.
courses.prerequisites: CS major and C or better in CS 1400 , or Data Science/ AI/ Computational Linguistics minor and C or better in CS 1260 ; MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , or MAT 1140 ; and STA 1200 , STA 1202 , STA 1300 , STA 2100 , or STA 2260 .

courses.title: Numerical Methods and Computing
courses.description: Linear algebra concepts, Linear Transformations and Matrix Factorizations, Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors, Least Squares, error analysis, floating-point representations, roots of non-linear equations, systems of linear equations, interpolation, numerical integration.
courses.prerequisites: CS major, and C or better in CS 2400 and MAT 1150 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Machine Learning and Its Applications
courses.description: Supervised learning techniques, including linear models for regression, linear models for classification, decision trees, support vector machines, neural networks. Unsupervised learning techniques, including clustering and dimensionality reduction. Related advanced topics. Case studies and applications.
courses.prerequisites: CS major and C or better in CS 3010 ; Data Science minor/ AI/ Computational Linguistics minor and C or better in CS 2410 ; Cybersecurity minor and C or better in CS 2400 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Big Data Analytics and Cloud Computing
courses.description: Data analytics lifecycle. Data analytics methods. Cloud infrastructure. Cloud storage, computing models and architectures. Big data and cloud security. Case studies.
courses.prerequisites: CS major or CS minor, and C or better in CS 2400 ; Data Science minor and C or better in CS 2410 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: College Algebra
courses.description: [GE 2] The theory and applications of real-valued functions, domain and range, compositions, inverses, transformations, equations and inequalities, and absolute value. Emphasis on polynomials, rational functions, power and root functions, piecewise functions, logarithms and exponential functions. Both symbolic and graphical representations of functions. Use of graphing devices to support reasoning about functions.
courses.prerequisites: Category I, Category II, ALEKS >=46, or C or better in a GE Sub-area 2/B4 course.

courses.title: Calculus I
courses.description: [GE 2] Functions, limits, continuity, derivatives of all functions including trigonometric, exponential, logarithmic, inverse trigonometric, and implicit functions. Applications of derivatives, including max/min problems and L’Hopitals rule. Definite and Indefinite Integrals, The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, substitution rule and applications.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in MAT 1050 and MAT 1060 ; C or better in MAT 1052 and MAT 1060 ; C or better in MAT 1055 and MAT 1060 ; C or better in MAT 1070 ; AP PreCalculus >=3; or ALEKS Comp >=76.

courses.title: Statistics with Applications
courses.description: [GE 2] Sample and population data; descriptive statistics, including numerical and graphical summarization of central tendency and spread; elementary probability, including events, basic probability rules, binomial and normal distributions; inferential statistics, including confidence intervals and hypothesis tests for one-population mean and proportion problems, simple linear regression and correlation
courses.prerequisites: Category I, Category II, ALEKS >=46, C or better in a GE Sub-area 2/B4 course, or C- or better or CR in MAT 1051 .

courses.title: Biostatistics
courses.description: [GE 2] Basic definitions, Sampling methods, Graphical display and descriptive statistics. Probability concepts, Normal distribution. Estimation, hypothesis testing, t-tests, goodness of fit, analysis of variance, regression and correlation, and nonparametric procedures. Applications in biological, agricultural, and other applied science. Use of computer packages for applied problems.
courses.prerequisites: Category I, Category II, MDPT >=14, ALEKS >=46, SAT >=570, ACT >=23, C or better in a GE Sub-area 2/B4 course, or C- or better or CR in MAT 1051 .

courses.title: Introduction to Statistics
courses.description: Population and sample data; random sampling; numerical and graphical summarization of data; basic probability concepts, including binomial and normal distributions; sampling distributions and the central limit theorem; point estimates, confidence intervals, and hypothesis tests for one- and two-sample mean and proportion problems; contingency tables and chi-squared tests; simple linear regression and correlation; one-way ANOVA; illustration with statistical software packages used throughout.
courses.prerequisites: AP Calc AB, AP Calc BC, MAT 1140 , MAT 1200 , MAT 1300 , MAT 1150 , or MAT 2140 .

courses.title: Probability and Statistics for Computer Scientists and Engineers
courses.description: Descriptive statistics. Rules of probability. Discrete and continuous probability distributions. Sampling distributions. Large- and small-sample inferences for one- and two-sample points. Interval Estimation and hypothesis testing for means, proportions and variances. Chi-Square tests. Analysis of variance. Introduction to regression and correlation.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in MAT 1150 or MAT 1310 .

courses.title: Senior Project
courses.description: Selection and completion of a project under faculty supervision. Projects typical of problems which graduates must solve in their fields of employment. Project results are presented in a formal report.
courses.prerequisites: Instructor consent.

courses.title: Senior Project
courses.description: Continuation of a project under faculty supervision with expectation of full project completion by the end of the term. Projects typical of problems which graduates must solve in their fields of employment. Project results are presented in a formal report.
courses.prerequisites: Instructor consent.

courses.title: Observational Astronomy
courses.description: An introduction to astrophysical data collection and analysis from both ground-based and space-based telescopes. Concepts, techniques, skills and resources needed to plan, obtain, reduce, and interpret astronomical observations across the electromagnetic spectrum. Corequisite(s): AST 3240A .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in PHY 1520 or PHY 133. Pre or Corequisite(s): C- or better in PHY 2530 or PHY 234.

courses.title: Observational Astronomy Computer Activity
courses.description: Computer based laboratory, with emphasis on data visualization and high-level programming skills. Completion of a data analysis project and submission of technical reports. Corequisite(s): AST 3240 .

courses.title: GIS Applications in Engineering and Remote Sensing
courses.description: GIS in engineering practice. Applications in environmental, water resources and transportation engineering. Spatial data structures (vector, raster). Data input and conversion. Terrain modeling and representation. Database management systems. Spatial and network analysis. Web mapping. Fundamentals of remote sensing. Radiation physics and spectral signatures. Radiation scattering. Image interpretation. Image processing. Ground truth data for quality assurance. Corequisite(s): CE 4331L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CE 134 or CE 1011 ; C- or better in CE 134L or CE 1011L ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: GIS Applications in Engineering and Remote Sensing Laboratory
courses.description: Data input and conversion. Spatial and network analysis. Digital image processing and interpretation. Project with civil engineering application.. Corequisite(s): CE 4331 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CE 134 or CE 1011 ; C- or better in CE 134L or CE 1011L ; and BSCE, BSCET, BSCEM, or MSCE Major.

courses.title: Business Intelligence
courses.description: Data Science cycle, data acquisition, questions and ideal data set, data cleaning, data compliance and security, data sharing, data visualization, data modeling, data analysis and dissemination of results. Storytelling for intelligence dissemination. Differences and similarities among descriptive analytics, data mining, web analytics and big data. Artificial intelligence and data science. IT governance. Business intelligence, data reporting, digital dashboards. Using data modeling for decision making, business analytics. Industry cases in marketing, finance, manufacturing, human resources. Future trends of business intelligence. Ethical and privacy issues. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in CIS 2100 , and junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Data Warehousing
courses.description: Designing large databases using advanced data modeling concepts. Producing quality data models which follow corporate business plans, policies, and strategies of the enterprise. Extracting information from different data sources to create data warehouses. Design infocubes. Use in-memory databases. Strategic use of data warehouses. Ethics and privacy challenges.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in CIS 325 or CIS 3252W , and CIS 2100 .

courses.title: Web and Mobile Analytics
courses.description: Web and mobile analytics studies the collection, analysis, and reporting of the audience, acquisition, behavior, and conversion data from websites and mobile applications, for the purposes of understanding and optimizing digital design, use, and performance. Advanced topics include data visualization, search engine optimization, attribution model, regular expression, tag management, conversion optimization, and the preparation for professional certification exams such as Google Analytics Individual Qualification (GAIQ) test.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in CIS 3252W .

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Business
courses.description: Fundamental Artificial Intelligence concepts and methods. Techniques and tools in Artificial Intelligence for business. Practical Artificial Intelligence applications in Business. Artificial Intelligence projects.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in CIS 2900 or CIS 2100 .

courses.title: Data Mining
courses.description: Data mining algorithms, machine learning to transform data into actionable knowledge. Business data mining projects.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in CIS 3252W and CIS 2100 .

courses.title: Big Data Analytics
courses.description: Concepts, techniques, and tools for big data analytics. Data analytics projects.
courses.prerequisites: CIS 2670 and CIS 4321 .

courses.title: Natural Language Processing and Time Series Analysis with Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Explores cutting-edge techniques and algorithms in advanced data analytics, focusing on text mining and time series analysis. Leveraging trends in Natural Language Processing (NLP), Large Language Models (LLMs), and AI, to extract valuable insights from unstructured text, time series, and geographic data and make predictive analyses. Through hands-on projects, applications include advanced AI-driven analytics to real-world business scenarios, enhancing skills in managing, processing, and interpreting data for actionable business intelligence. Advanced algorithms, concepts, techniques, and skills in business analytics. Data analytics projects.
courses.when_offered: As needed; see Academic Department, Fall, Spring, Summer, Winter

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Overview of the different application areas of AI. Introduction to the basic AI concepts and techniques such as heuristic search, knowledge representation, automated reasoning. In-depth discussion of several AI application areas: their specific problems, tools and techniques.
courses.prerequisites: CS major or CS minor, and C or better in CS 2400 ; or Data Science/ AI/ Computational Linguistics minor and C or better in CS 2410 .

courses.title: Graphics Processing Unit Computing
courses.description: Programming massively parallel processors on Graphics Processing Unit (GPU). Heterogeneous data parallel computing, multidimensional grids and data, compute architecture and scheduling, memory architecture and data locality, performance considerations, parallel patterns, and advanced patterns and applications.
courses.prerequisites: CS major, and C or better in CS 2600 and CS 2640 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Social Computing
courses.description: Representing, modeling, processing and analyzing social information. Graph based techniques for social network analysis, community detection, influence spread and centrality analysis. Models for application domains such as social media, epidemiology, and political science. Parallel and distributed tools for large scale modeling and analysis.
courses.prerequisites: CS major or CS minor, and C or better in CS 2400 ; Data Science minor and C or better in CS 2410 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Web Search and Recommender Systems
courses.description: Web Search engine architectures, techniques, and technologies. Web crawling. Web document processing, Link analysis, and ranking. Introduction to retrieval models. Search engine optimization. Web search user interfaces. Recommender Systems. Evaluation. Current trends.
courses.prerequisites: CS major or CS minor, and C or better in CS 2400 ; Data Science/ Artificial Intelligence/ Computational Linguistics minor and C or better in CS 2410 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Database Systems
courses.description: Database and transaction systems. Database components. Database design and constraints. Normalization theory. Data modeling. Relational and object data models. Relational algebra and calculus. SQL programming paradigms. Concurrency control, crush recovery, and security.
courses.prerequisites: CS major or CS minor, and C or better in CS 2400 ; Data Science minor and C or better in CS 2410 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Data Mining
courses.description: An end-to-end view of data mining, covering data acquisition, preparation, and analysis using various algorithms. Explore data types, attributes, storage, and perform exploratory data analysis with statistical techniques and visualization. Topics include pattern mining, clustering, classification, and outlier detection. Ethical considerations and applications of data mining are also discussed.
courses.prerequisites: CS major and C or better in CS 2400 ; Data Science/ ArtificiaI Intelligence/ Computational Linguistics minor and C or better in CS 2410 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Cloud Computing Practicum with Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud Platform, and Microsoft Azure
courses.description: Intro to Cloud Architecture and Amazon Web Services (AWS) Platform, Google Cloud Platform (GCP) and Microsoft Azure. AWS Networking and Virtual Private Cloud (VPC). Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3). Amazon Elastic Computing (E3B/C2). Databases on AWS, GCP and Azure. Identity and Access Management (IAM) in AWS. Deploying Cloud Application on AWS, GCP and Azure.
courses.prerequisites: CS major or CS minor, and C or better in CS 2400 ; Data Science minor and C or better in CS 2410 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Prompt Engineering
courses.description: A comprehensive introduction to prompt engineering, focusing on designing effective prompts for Large Language Models (LLMs). Students will explore essential concepts, including LLM foundations, interactive prompts, and parameter tuning. Various prompt patterns and templates, customization and fine-tuning techniques, and methods for evaluating prompt effectiveness are covered. Ethical considerations and security aspects in prompt engineering will also be discussed. Additionally, learn to apply prompt engineering in specialized domains through hands-on development, gaining practical experience in building AI-powered applications.
courses.prerequisites: CS major/ CS minor/ Cybersecurity minor and C or better in CS 2400 ; Data Science/ Computational Linguistic/ AI minor and C or better in CS 2410 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Data Analysis: Application in Industrial and Systems Engineering
courses.description: Gain both theoretical understanding and hands-on experience using AI tools to enhance efficiency, productivity, and innovation in industrial and manufacturing systems. An in-depth exploration of artificial intelligence (AI) methodologies and their practical applications in the fields of industrial and manufacturing engineering. Learn foundational concepts in machine learning, deep learning, and data-driven decision-making, with a focus on solving real-world problems in manufacturing, supply chain optimization, process automation, and predictive maintenance. Key AI topics covered, such as data collection and preprocessing, regression techniques, supervised and unsupervised learning, and reinforcement learning. Special emphasis will be placed on the integration of deep learning models, including neural networks and transformers, in industrial engineering applications.
courses.prerequisites: IME 3140 or IME 3150 , and IME 2130L .

courses.title: GIS Programing
courses.description: Fundamental concepts in programing languages used in GIS. Focus on GIS script writing for frequently occurring tasks in customization and application development within a GIS system. Corequisite(s): GEO 3220L .
courses.prerequisites: GEO 2400 and GEO 2400L , or consent of instructor.

courses.title: GIS Programing Laboratory
courses.description: Fundamental concepts in programing languages used in GIS. Focus on GIS script writing for frequently occurring tasks in customization and application development within a GIS system. Corequisite(s): GEO 3220 .
courses.prerequisites: GEO 2400 and GEO 2400L , or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Geodemographics with Geographic Information Systems
courses.description: Application of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) techniques for the analysis of spatial and locational patterns of human population, population characteristics and population change. Housing, migration and commuting patterns. Market analysis and site location decision support. Neighborhood segregation and transitions. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement. Corequisite(s): GEO 4050LW .
courses.prerequisites: GEO 2400 , GEO 2400L , and junior or senior standing, or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Remote Sensing of the Environment
courses.description: Principles and techniques of remote sensing using remotely sensed data to examine physical and cultural geographic scenes. Remote sensing applications in urban planning, agriculture, ecosystem management, atmosphere and earth sciences, and geographic information systems. Corequisite(s): GEO 4100L .
courses.prerequisites: GEO 2400 and GEO 2400L or Instructor consent.

courses.title: Remote Sensing of the Environment Laboratory
courses.description: Principles and techniques of remote sensing using remotely sensed data to examine physical and cultural geographic scenes. Remote sensing applications in urban planning, agriculture, ecosystem management, atmosphere and earth sciences, and geographic information systems. Corequisite(s): GEO 4100 .
courses.prerequisites: GEO 2400 and GEO 2400L .

courses.title: Advanced GIS
courses.description: Technical issues of geographic information systems. Topics include: data structures, database models, error estimation, and product generation. 3 hours lecture/problem-solving. Corequisite(s): GEO 4400L .
courses.prerequisites: GEO 2400 and GEO 2400L or Instructor consent.

courses.title: Advanced GIS Laboratory
courses.description: Technical issues of geographic information systems. Topics include: data structures, database models, error estimation, and product generation. 3 hours laboratory. Corequisite(s): GEO 4400 .
courses.prerequisites: GEO 2400 and GEO 2400L .

courses.title: Geospatial Data Analysis
courses.description: Quantitative analysis methods for research in the spatial sciences. Characteristics of geographic data (attributes of objects and fields in geographic space). Probability, hypothesis testing and confidence intervals. Summary, descriptive and exploratory statistics for geographic data. Regression modeling. Spatial autocorrelation and spatial regression methods. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement. Corequisite(s): GEO 4430LW .
courses.prerequisites: GEO 2400 , GEO 2400L , and junior or senior standing; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Applied Regression Analysis
courses.description: Simple linear regression and scatterplots, multiple linear regression, matrix formulation of regression, least squares estimation, interpretation of regression coefficients, hypothesis tests for regression coefficients, confounding and multicollinearity, interaction and effect modification, regression diagnostics and remedial measures, model selection, use of statistical software packages for all techniques discussed.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing; OR C or better in STA 2100 , STA 2260 , TOM 3020 , EC 3322 , or IME 3140; and C or better in MAT 2240 and MAT 2250 .

courses.title: Categorical Data Analysis
courses.description: Contingency Tables, Odds ratio, Fisher’s exact tests, Chi-square tests, M-tests, Generalized Linear Models including logistic regression and Poisson regression.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in STA 2100 , STA 2260 , TOM 3020 , EC 3322 , or IME 3140.

courses.title: Business Analytics
courses.description: Overview of business analytics. Problem framing. Categorization of analytical methods and models. Descriptive analytics and data visualization. Predictive analytics including data mining and simulation. Prescriptive analytics including optimization. Decision analysis. Spreadsheet implementation.
courses.prerequisites: TOM 302 or TOM 3020 .
